title: One recorded source transition
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $y$. Suppose a Boolean tag $b$ correctly marks the boundary position of $c$'s input head, and let $n$ be a family of natural-number movement counts, indexed by the fields of a stored row, such that each count's binary representation has length at most $W$. For any record word and natural numbers $T,t,W$, there are a natural number $s \le 2W+5$ and a Boolean tag $b'$ correctly marking the input-head position after one step of $M$, such that the recorder, started in its source-release control with configuration $c$, counts $n$, record, clock budget $T$, and logical time $t$, reaches its next row-copy control with source configuration $M(c)$, counts advanced by one on exactly the counters selected by that transition's signed head movements, and the same record, clock budget, and logical time.
hypotheses_covered: finite Boolean-alphabet machine $M$; Boolean words $x,y$; source configuration $c$ on $y$
tag $b$ satisfies the virtual-boundary tag condition for $c$'s input-head position
movement-count family $n$ indexed by the stored-row fields
every count in $n$ has binary length at most $W$
replaced: Let $c$ be a source configuration with a valid position tag, and let the movement counts have binary representations of width at most $W$. From the source-release phase, there is a time $s \le 2W + 5$ after which the recorder has executed exactly one source transition together with its full signed counter update and dispatched to the next row-copy phase, with a valid tag for the stepped configuration; the record and clock contents and heads are framed throughout.
